decisions.reason: As an established extension of the firm's psychiatric and therapeutic core that has remained on offer into a second year, it is likely to meet aspiration levels well enough to retain.
Custom furniture is more peripheral to the core care business, but its link to workshop activity and continued organisational expansion make continued support more likely than withdrawal.
Outpatient sociotherapy is close to the firm's established support services, so management would usually keep it while accumulating evidence rather than redeploying resources quickly.
The service fits the firm's senior-care capabilities closely and its earlier prominence suggests it has stayed above aspiration thresholds for continuation.
The retail shop is less central than direct care services but remains mission-linked as an outlet for sheltered-workshop activity, which supports keeping it despite some performance uncertainty.

Meal delivery for seniors is close to the firm's eldercare offer, and although it is still relatively new and operationally demanding, an expanding organisation is likely to continue it while learning about demand.
